disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the New Mexico Department of Game and Fish before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.public_land_trapping_ban: Under Roxy's Law (NMSA section 17-11-1), traps and snares are illegal on public land, with narrow exceptions: cage traps may be used to abate damage to property, crops, or livestock, and enrolled members of a federally recognized Indian nation, tribe, or pueblo may use traps or snares solely for religious or ceremonial purposes.
license_summary.trapping_license: A New Mexico trapper license is required. Consult the NMDGF booklet for license types, fees, and trap registration/check requirements.

sources.notes: 2026–27 New Mexico Hunting Rules and Info booklet, Furbearers section (pages 131–133). All season dates, Roxy's Law public-land ban, the no-bag-limit rule, the closed species list, and the Canada lynx release/report rule read directly from this booklet. Archived locally in hidden_files/season-research/.

verification.confirmation_notes: 2026–27 New Mexico Hunting Rules and Info booklet (Furbearers, pages 131–133) verified 2026-09-18. All season dates read directly from the table, including the Raccoon - restricted methods row. Roxy's Law public-land trap/snare ban, no-bag-limit rule, beaver public-land closure in the Cibola/Lincoln/Gila National Forests, and the lynx release/report rule confirmed in the booklet.
known_gaps: The booklet prints 'May 16–August 31, 2027' for Raccoon - restricted methods — after the license year ends. Reproduced verbatim with a warning; NOT corrected to 2026, because guessing a date is not allowed.
Scientific names are standard taxonomy, NOT stated in the NMDGF booklet — all flagged scientific_name_verified=false; fox, weasel, and skunks are null because the booklet is generic.
The beaver National Forest closure is modeled descriptively — the app cannot resolve exact public-land boundaries.
Depredation trapping under Roxy's Law exceptions (cage traps for damage abatement; tribal religious/ceremonial use) is noted in the license summary, not modeled as a season.
